extracted.intended_audience: general newspaper readers / journalists interested in international and political news
extracted.subtask_description: Compilation of wire-service international news briefs and analysis items covering diplomacy, conflict, economic institutions, and government actions; typical of a newspaper's international news homepage or wire digest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstention from repeated threats
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed by U.N. Secretary-General Dag Hammarskjold as one of the unilateral moves by parties that could improve the tense Palestine situation; presented as a specific behavioral standard for governments to reduce escalation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respect for demilitarized zones (1949 armistice agreement)
rubrics_metrics.description: “Respect for demilitarized zones set up in the 1949 armistice agreement.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hammarskjold criticized governments for lack of cooperation and failure to enforce discipline upon their forces; respecting demilitarized zones is presented as a concrete requirement to forestall incidents and uphold cease-fire arrangements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Freedom of navigation in the Suez Canal for Israeli ships
rubrics_metrics.description: “Freedom for Israeli navigation in the Suez Canal as called for by a Council resolution of Sept. 1, 1951.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommended by the Secretary-General as a measure to improve conditions; the article notes Israel claims Egypt bars ships trading with Israeli ports while Egypt asserts a right to restrict passage for defense—contextualizes the standard and its contested implementation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strict adherence to the cease-fire
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of the Secretary-General's recommended unilateral moves; emphasizes enforcing no‑shooting agreements and discipline of forces to prevent incidents that could undermine the armistice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Repatriation and resettlement of Palestine-war refugees
rubrics_metrics.description: “Repatriation and resettlement of almost a million Arab Palestine-war refugees now living largely on relief in Arab countries bordering Israel.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Framed as a necessary humanitarian/political measure to help stabilize the region; one of the Secretary-General's concrete policy recommendations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Utilization of Jordan waters / water‑sharing plans
rubrics_metrics.description: “Utilization of Jordan waters,” for which water‑sharing plans are still pending.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identified as a cooperative technical/political step that could improve relations and reduce tensions; presented as pending but recommended.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use competitive bidding to the greatest degree practicable
rubrics_metrics.description: “Competitive bidding to the greatest degree practicable.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stated by the Navy in describing procurement for submarine propulsion equipment (Westinghouse contract); presented as the procurement policy/standard to be followed when purchasing equipment from industry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permitted activities for foreign election observers
rubrics_metrics.description: Visitors would be permitted to tour the country, attending political rallies, hearing campaign speeches and finally watching actual balloting process on Nov. 6.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describes the intended scope of privileges for foreign observers invited by the U.S. State Department as part of a cultural exchange/election‑observation program: arrival dates, duration (~three weeks), and expenses paid by the U.S. government.

rubrics_metrics.name: Official visas for Communist observers (no fingerprinting)
rubrics_metrics.description: Communist election observers would get “official visas” which do not require fingerprinting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains a policy/assumption behind the invitations: offering official visas (no fingerprinting) to avoid diplomatic friction, noting that Communist governments have objected to fingerprinting in the past.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitor and guard against persistent inflationary pressures
rubrics_metrics.description: The Fund advised its members to beware of strong inflationary pressures — not a runaway inflation but a persistent rise in prices and costs — calling for constant watchfulness over money and credit expansion as well as government programs of spending and investment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IMF/World Bank guidance to member governments: continual monitoring and macroeconomic policy measures to prevent and manage sustained inflationary trends.

rubrics_metrics.name: Liberalized lending and rule changes for small/less‑developed countries
rubrics_metrics.description: Small‑country governments asked for a liberalized lending attitude as well as rule changes which would make it easier for the smaller countries to borrow.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Delegates (led by Cuba and Jordan) criticized the Bank as overly conservative and called for policy changes to increase access to development loans for less‑developed countries; presented as a policy desideratum for international lending institutions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditionality of arms shipments on geopolitical tensions
rubrics_metrics.description: If tension between Arab countries and Israel worsens, the shipments can be stopped.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statement by the Canadian Prime Minister regarding permission to sell 24 Canadian Sabre jets to Israel; frames arms exports as subject to suspension if regional tensions rise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corroboration and reexamination of informant testimony
rubrics_metrics.description: The Justice Department asked the Supreme Court to remand a case because post‑trial sworn statements by an informant (Joseph D. Mazzei) raised serious doubt as to his veracity; the Department said Mazzei's testimony had been checked and corroborated as far as possible at trial but later statements conflicted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implied standard for prosecutions: ensure informant testimony is corroborated and reexamine convictions if substantial post‑trial questions about a witness's truthfulness emerge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judicial practice of telescoping concurrent sentences
rubrics_metrics.description: Court custom: giving multiple maximum terms but ‘telescoping them into a single five year term by providing that they be served concurrently, rather than consecutively.’
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describes a sentencing practice used by the judge in the Matusow perjury conviction; presented as an established courtroom practice for imposing multiple counts' penalties.
